title: tern: elevation profile SVG in progress, RDP downsample next

projectIdentity.summary: tern is a small CLI (package.json name "tern", version 0.3.0) that turns GPX hiking tracks into printable trip sheets: one A5 page per leg, monochrome, meant to be carried on the trail. Source lives under src/, currently two files: gpx.js (track reading and distance) and sheet.js (sheet rendering).

decisions.summary: 1. All distances are integer meters end to end; kilometers exist only at render time. Reason: accumulating floating-point kilometers made long-track totals disagree with the GPS device readout by tens of meters, and hikers noticed. Confirmed in code: src/gpx.js's legDistanceMeters rounds each haversine segment to whole meters before summing, and src/sheet.js only converts to km (toFixed(1)) at the point of building the printed line. 2. Trip sheets are rendered with plain template strings, no template engine. Reason: the engine considered would have been the project's only heavy dependency, for two pages of monospaced text. Confirmed in code: src/sheet.js is a single template-literal array joined with newlines, and package.json lists no dependencies at all.

architecture.summary: Two source files exist under src/: gpx.js (readTrack for parsing trkpt lat/lon out of GPX XML text, legDistanceMeters and haversineMeters for integer-meter distance) and sheet.js (renderSheet, the plain-template-string sheet layout). package.json's bin field points to src/cli.js, but that file does not exist in the repository - unchecked whether it was removed, never committed, or is planned but not yet started. Vocabulary: a "leg" is the stretch between two named waypoints; the "book" is the set of sheets for one trip.

constraints.summary: A trip sheet must stay legible on A5 monochrome paper, because it is carried on the trail. Nothing that only reads in color. This bears directly on the elevation-profile SVG: it needs to read at A5 size in black and white (line weight and fill pattern, not color, for any distinction it needs to draw).

rejectedPaths.summary: Parsing GPX with regular expressions was rejected as the long-term approach: it misread Garmin's namespaced extension elements (gpxtpx:*), so a small streaming XML tokenizer is the plan instead. The regex is still in place today as an explicit placeholder (src/gpx.js line 6, commented "placeholder until tokenizer lands") and matches only trkpt lat/lon attributes - it has not yet been swapped for the tokenizer.

executiveSummary.summary: The project is early: two source files, one commit ("wip"), working tree clean. GPX parsing and leg distance in meters both work with a placeholder regex tokenizer. Sheet rendering emits plain-text template output with a spot reserved for an inline elevation-profile SVG (leg.profileSvg), but that SVG is not generated anywhere yet: sheet.js falls back to the literal string "(elevation profile pending)" when it is absent. The immediate task is building that per-leg elevation profile, and the agreed next step before drawing it is Ramer-Douglas-Peucker downsampling.

currentTask.summary: Build the per-leg elevation profile as inline SVG on the trip sheet. In code today, sheet.js's renderSheet expects a leg.profileSvg string and falls back to a placeholder line if it is missing (src/sheet.js line 11: leg.profileSvg ?? "(elevation profile pending)"). No function that produces profileSvg exists yet in either src/gpx.js or src/sheet.js: the profile generator and the SVG-drawing code have not been written. This confirms the profile work is at the start of implementation, not partway through.
